judgements.justification: Created by this pair: all four B reviewers held the analysis study to a design-guidance test that A did not apply, and A's qxEj counted design inspiration as a strength.
No reviewer's praise rests on a wrong factual claim; qxEj's 7 is thin praise, not a factual error, and SJG2's batch-norm error did not raise a score.
sCgD said several concerns were addressed but kept an above-threshold 6; B's below-threshold 16Eb and fR12 did not concede their main concerns were resolved.
The authors offered arguments, not promised experiments, on the CNN choice; neither committee was asked to credit promised revisions.
MKzA's comment 'I rate the score to 6' matches its edited rating; no stated stance diverged from a score.
B's AC cites private comments not in the record, but no additional late reviewer was called in to break the split.
Neither committee's verdict turned on clarity judged by reviewer distance from the field; both found the paper clear.
No reviewer raised a score silently; MKzA's possible change came with a stated reason, and its earlier score is unknown.
Neither AC discounted a rating for silence; A's silent qxEj and SJG2 and B's silent NaL7 all counted.
A had no reviewer rating well above threshold on a detailed reading who argued for the paper; its 7s are a brief review and a praise-only one.
No reviewer admitted reading only part of the paper.
Both committees accepted the CKA-analysis framing; no reviewer contested the premise from another tradition.
A's meta-review argued only acceptance ('A good paper on a timely topic. All reviewers recommend acceptance.') and gave no reason for the spotlight.
NaL7 noted three uncited concurrent works in a two-sentence review, but no B reviewer checked results against published ones, and A probed the method rather than taking comparisons at face value.
B's AC wrote that 'the reviewers all said' the study was not thorough on other CNNs; only 16Eb and fR12 raised it, and fR12 and MKzA called the analysis thorough, in the direction of reject.
No reviewer or AC in either committee said the paper interests few readers or suits another venue.
The misreading detractor (16Eb) was in B, which rejected; A had no such detractor and the tier gap does not come from a chair defending acceptance.
A received new channel-normalized heatmaps, but no A score rose on them; the scores in A did not move.
No committee had a lone high-confidence expert outweighed; B's confidence-5 NaL7 wrote a two-sentence review, and A's confidence-5 qGAU rated 7.
No objection or score change came after the author response period in either committee.
The gap reflects different standards (design guidance, one CNN family), not similar verbal assessments scored on different scales.
sCgD noted the 'representative set of CNN' wording, but no committee held the paper to a lower tier for an overstated headline claim; B rejected on design utility and generality.
A's 6s came from detailed, critical reviews and A still gave a spotlight; no unsure reviewers' flat marginal scores set a poster-level verdict.
